intended_object: The largest eigenvalue of the symmetric Hamming Jacobi matrix `hammingJacobiMatrix n k L`, indexed by Fin (L-k+1), used in a spectral (linear-programming style) bound on binary codes. It is given through the Rayleigh–Ritz characterisation, the supremum of the Rayleigh quotient over nonzero vectors. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the lemmas proved about it.
explanation: The body takes the real supremum, over nonzero x, of `ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient` for the operator `Matrix.toEuclideanLin (matrix n k L)`. The library proves this matrix is Hermitian. For a symmetric operator on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, this supremum is the largest eigenvalue (Rayleigh–Ritz). The library confirms that it is an eigenvalue using Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.hasEigenvalue_iSup_of_finiteDimensional`. The index type Fin (L-k+1) always has at least one element, so nonzero vectors exist. The Rayleigh quotients are bounded by the operator norm (`rayleigh_bddAbove`). So the supremum takes no junk value. The object is one specific number attached to one specific matrix, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no named definition of "the top eigenvalue", only the iSup lemma and `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues`, which lists all eigenvalues.
